summary: Shows copy examples: owner, group, and octal or symbolic modes; backing up the original; validating sudoers with visudo; copying on the remote with remote_src; inline content; and how `follow` affects copying onto a symlink.
questions: How do I safely copy a sudoers file?
Can you show copy with owner, group and mode?
How do I copy over a symlink without replacing the link itself?
How do I copy a remote file to a new name on the same host?
How do I write a one-line file with copy?

answer_card.title: copy module examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: /srv/myfiles/foo.conf
    dest: /etc/foo.conf
    owner: foo
    group: foo
    mode: '0644'            # or u=rw,g=r,o=r / u+rw,g-wx,o-rwx

- ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: /mine/ntp.conf
    dest: /etc/ntp.conf
    backup: yes

- ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: /mine/sudoers
    dest: /etc/sudoers
    validate: /usr/sbin/visudo -csf %s

- ansible.builtin.copy:      # copy on the remote machine
    src: /etc/sudoers
    dest: /etc/sudoers.edit
    remote_src: yes

- ansible.builtin.copy:
    content: '# This file was moved to /etc/other.conf'
    dest: /etc/mine.conf
```
With `dest` a symlink: `follow: yes` overwrites the link's target file; `follow: no` turns the link into a regular file.
